principle_text: When the persuadee responds with simple acknowledgment without engagement, avoid asking questions that only elicit minimal confirmation without advancing the donation conversation.
When the persuadee is familiar with a charity and willing to engage, you should emphasize the meaningful impact of the cause to inspire immediate commitment to donate.
When the persuadee shows willingness to donate, you should ask a direct question about the donation amount to encourage commitment and clarify their intent.
When the persuadee commits to a donation amount, you should positively reinforce their generosity to increase their enthusiasm and engagement.
When the persuadee acknowledges logistical information positively, avoid merely stating process details without linking them to increased motivation or donation commitment.
When the persuadee expresses general concern or thoughtfulness about the cause, avoid vague appeals that do not clearly connect their feelings to specific donation actions.

When the persuadee responds playfully or with humor that does not reinforce the donation goal, avoid relying solely on optimistic or inspirational statements without connecting them to concrete benefits.
When the persuadee responds with humor or unrelated comments, avoid shifting the topic abruptly without linking it back to the donation purpose to maintain focus and engagement.
When the persuadee responds with neutral or uncertain statements, avoid merely acknowledging their contribution without encouraging deeper engagement or reinforcing the impact of their donation.
